question.text: The last sovereign emperor of the Inca was this son of Huayna Capac. who was strangled to death after providing the conquistador Francisco Pizarro with a room filled once with gold and twice with silver.
question.clue: He offered to fill a large room with gold and silver for his ransom, but the Spaniards didn't release him.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the native peoples of the Americas.
swap.text: This civilization, with capital at Cuzco and another city at Macchu Picchu, was conquered by Francisco Pizarro.
swap.clue: Descendants of this empire's royalty included Garcilaso de la Vega, and this empire was sometimes named for the four administrative suyus that it was divided into.

question.leadin: Answer the following about indigenous peoples of South America.
question.text: The Quechua group, who share their name with the language of the Inca Empire, live in and around this mountain range in Peru, Ecuador, and Bolivia.
question.clue: A culture in this mountain range depicted a spider called the "Decapitator" and created a mummy known as the Lord of Sipan.

swap.text: Identify the Spaniard who conquered the Incan Empire.
swap.clue: This man received help from longtime partner Diego Almagro, but he was killed by Almagro's forces in the Battle of Las Salinas.

question.leadin: The "trophy heads" collected by this culture featured a hole in the skull where a rope was threaded through.
question.text: Name this culture who created geoglyphs in the shape of condors and hummingbirds in the desert, known as their namesake "lines."
question.clue: This culture built the Cantalloc ("cahn-TAH-yoke")Aqueducts, exemplifying the corkscrew entrances of their puquios ("poo-KEE-ohʼs").

swap.text: Paul Kosok discovered the Hummingbird, an earthwork built by these people indigenous to Peru. These people built the city of Cahuachi [ca-WA-chee] and used puquios to irrigate their crops.
swap.clue: Paul Kosok and Maria Reiche (RAI-keh) mapped structures created by these people.

question.leadin: This country is home to a Maoist cell called Shining Path, whose crackdown led to many human rights abuses by its ethnically Japanese president Alberto Fujimori in the 90s.
question.text: Name this country whose navy was beaten by nearby Chile in the War of the Pacific. This country just got back a trove of artifacts that Yale stole from Machu Picchu.
question.clue: That culture in this country was also responsible for creating a series of images called Lines near Palpa that are well-known geoglyphs.

swap.leadin: It was conquered by Francisco Pizarro in 1533 after the battle of Cajamarca, which Jared Diamond wrote on in Guns, Germs, and Steel.
swap.text: Name this South American empire which built stone roads up and down the length of Andes mountains.
swap.answerHtml: Incan empire [accept Tawantinsuyu even though that was the word the Inca used for the entire known world]
swap.clue: The final leaders of this empire ruled from Vilcabamba, and legend teaches that it was founded by Manco Capac.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about pivotal ships from world history.
question.text: This ship participated in most major engagements in Peruvian history during the latter half of the nineteenth century. It was named for the brother of Incan ruler Atahualpa.
question.clue: This Peruvian ship sank the Esmeralda before Chile captured it in the War of the Pacific. It took its name from an Incan noble who lost a civil war to his brother Atahualpa.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain precious metal in pre-Columbian South America.
swap.text: One of the leaders of this confederation ritually covered himself in gold dust before diving into Lake Guatavita. This confederation, which was led by a Zipa and a Zaque ["ZAH-kay"], held territory in the highlands of modern-day Colombia.
swap.clue: Perhaps this polity's most well-known artefact is known as this polity's "raft", which is a gold sculpture that was found in Lake Guatavita.

question.text: Conquistadors high off chivalric fantasies searched for this mythical city of gold inspired by Muisca folklore.
question.clue: During the first part of the journey in which Orellana travelled the length of the Amazon, a valley of Cinnamon and this place were the targets of Gonzalo Pizzaro.

swap.text: Incan relay messengers, the chasquis, carried messages via these "talking knots" that were made of llama hair.
swap.clue: This devices that were made of string and were commonly used for keeping census records or for monitoring taxes. The information on these devices was stored using knots.

question.text: This country commissioned the Almirante Grau-class cruisers during that arms race, named after this country's admiral Miguel Grau. This country and an eastern ally were defeated by a southern neighbor in a war that was sparked by the institution of a nitrate tax.
question.clue: The Marxist Shining Path rebels fought against the government of this country, which became a dictatorship in the years following Alberto Fujimori's electoral victory over Mario Vargas Llosa.

swap.leadin: The former MIT student Lori Berenson was accused of collaborating with a modern organization named for this person.
swap.text: Identify this man who names a "Revolutionary Movement" led by Victor Campos. This Indigenous rebel, who took his name from a monarch executed at Vilcabamba, was defeated at the 1780 Battle of Sangarara.
swap.answerHtml: Túpac Amaru II [in place of “Túpac” accept Thupaq or Thupa or Topa; in place of “Amaru” accept Amaro; accept Túpac Amaru Revolutionary Movement; prompt on José Gabriel Condorcanqui by asking “what name did he adopt?”; prompt on MRTA]
swap.clue: This leader's revolt targeted the expansion of the alcabala and a system of forced mining labour called the mit'a.

question.leadin: According to one crackpot theory, these structures were built using medieval hot-air balloons.
question.text: Name these massive desert drawings that have been hypothesized to represent constellations. Greenpeace activists managed to damage one shaped like a hummingbird in late 2014.
question.answerHtml: Nazca Lines [accept Lines and Geoglyphs of Nasca and Palpa, accept Lineas de Nazca]
question.clue: These things were damaged by Greenpeace activists wearing improper footwear as part of a 2014 protest.

swap.text: The original "Maritime Foundations" theory was developed after the excavation of this site at the mouth of the Supe River that likely provided fish to Caral from the nearby ocean. This place is the type site of the Norte Chico.

question.text: The Larco Museum exhibits condor-head cups from this altiplano state. The Urus of Lake Titicaca's reed islands may have adopted the Puquina ("poo-kee-nah") language from this state, which built the Bennett Monolith and Gate of the Sun.
question.clue: This city, which also had productive raised fields called "suka qullu" ("KOO-loo"). The island of Pariti was an important pilgrimage site for this city's residents, who also built the Pumapunku complex.

swap.leadin: This cloud forest culture created mosaic friezes at Gran Pajaten ("pa-ha-TEN"), built cliff tombs at Revash, and produced the Laguna de Los Condores textiles.
swap.text: Name this culture that built the walled city of Kuelap in Amazonas, Peru. This culture's people were ascribed white skin by Inca chroniclers, whose reports of their ferocity inspired their nickname of "warriors of the clouds."

question.leadin: The Met holds a work made of this material with French lettering and scenes from Greek mythology, and a lliklla ("LEEK-l'yah") made of this material that imitates Spanish-style lattice motifs.
question.text: Name this material used to make low-quality awasqa or high-quality qunpi ("COMB-pee"), decorated with tukapu motifs. A red llawt'u ("l'YAO-too") decorated the maskhaypacha, an imperial symbol made of this material.
question.answerHtml: camelid wool [or millma or millwa or willma; accept camelid hair or camelid fur; accept fleece in place of “wool”; accept llama, alpaca, or vicuña in place of “camelid”; prompt on hair or fur; prompt on textile or fabric or clothing or p’achakuna by asking “made of what substance?”; prompt on cotton or utkhu by asking “what material is more commonly used?”; reject “rope” or “chord”]

swap.leadin: This system was instituted by the Spanish in 1573 to draft people to work the mines of Potosi.
swap.text: Identify this form of labor tax which used by the Incans for such infrastructure projects as the construction of the extensive network of roads.
swap.clue: Las Casas would likely not have approved of the Spanish adoption of this Incan labor system which allowed them to conscript natives for public service work.
